items.title: 🔋 THE LITHIUM BOOM CAME BACK. THE LITHIUM PROFITS DIDN'T. China's battery chain earned ~Rmb64bn in 2Q26. That beats the 2022 peak. Citi just showed...
items.description_html:
🔋 THE LITHIUM BOOM CAME BACK. THE LITHIUM PROFITS DIDN'T.

China's battery chain earned ~Rmb64bn in 2Q26. That beats the 2022 peak. Citi just showed where it went.

4Q22 vs 2Q26, same ~Rmb60bn of chain EBIT:

• Lithium: ~Rmb30bn → ~Rmb17bn
• Battery makers (ex BYD): ~Rmb14bn → ~Rmb28bn
• Everyone else: roughly flat

Miners lost half their take. Cell makers doubled theirs.

• 🔥 Record chain profit ≠ Record mining profit
• 🔥 Lithium price spike ≠ Lithium margin spike
• 🔥 Most capacity ≠ Most profit

The bottleneck moved. In 2022 nobody could get lithium. In 2026 nobody can match the cell makers' scale and cost.

Caveat: lithium's share rose in 2Q26 at the expense of cathode and cells, so the miners are clawing some back. Two more quarters decide it.

items.title: 🚨 AI DEMAND IS BOOMING. DATA CENTER STOCKS ARE FALLING. WHAT IS WALL STREET MISSING? GDS fell 20%. VNET plunged 29%. All while AI infrastructure de...
items.description_html:
🚨 AI DEMAND IS BOOMING. DATA CENTER STOCKS ARE FALLING. WHAT IS WALL STREET MISSING?

GDS fell 20%. VNET plunged 29%.

All while AI infrastructure demand remained strong.

GS' 9 October research raises an uncomfortable question:

WHO IS ACTUALLY EARNING THEIR COST OF CAPITAL?

The economics tell a fascinating story:

🔴 Powered Shells: ~5% ROIC. Predictable revenues, but limited returns.

🟠 GPU-as-a-Service: Moderate-to-high ROIC potential. Massive capex and GPU obsolescence risk.

🟢 AI Token Factories: High ROIC potential. But token pricing, utilization and technology risks could destroy margins.

The biggest investing trap?

🔥 AI demand ≠ Shareholder returns

🔥 Full capacity ≠ Profitable capacity

🔥 Revenue growth ≠ Value creation

🔥 Cheap financing ≠ Strong underlying ROIC

Remember the telecom boom?

The internet changed the world. Yet Global Crossing collapsed in 2002 under $12.4 billion of debt.

The technology was transformative. The capital allocation was disastrous.

AI infrastructure investors face a similar question today.

Goldman highlights three levers for improving shareholder economics:

• Cheap financing: Range Intelligent secured RMB3bn of debt at just 1.65%.

• Capital recycling: REIT structures can release trapped capital.

• Global expansion: Higher rental markets could improve returns.

But here's the catch:

Financial engineering can improve equity returns. It cannot magically turn poor operating economics into great economics.

Wall Street counts GPUs and megawatts.

Smart investors count ROIC, WACC and free cash flow.

The next AI investment battle won't simply be about who builds the most capacity.

It will be about WHO CREATES THE MOST VALUE PER DOLLAR INVESTED.

items.title: 🚨 WALL STREET LOVES AI HYPE. BUT HYPE DOESN'T PAY SHAREHOLDERS! Citi Research shows AI Adopters, AI Enablers, Cloud Computing and Cybersecurity amo...
items.description_html:
🚨 WALL STREET LOVES AI HYPE. BUT HYPE DOESN'T PAY SHAREHOLDERS!

Citi Research shows AI Adopters, AI Enablers, Cloud Computing and Cybersecurity among the themes with the lowest idiosyncratic risk.

But low idiosyncratic risk doesn't mean low systemic or market-wide risk!

The investing trap?

🔥 Great technology ≠ Great investment

🔥 Explosive growth ≠ Shareholder returns

🔥 Innovation ≠ Profitability

🔥 Low company-specific risk ≠ Protection from a market crash

🔥 Market leadership ≠ Attractive valuation

Remember the dot-com bubble? The internet changed the world, but many investors still lost fortunes.

AI could transform businesses without rewarding every AI stock investor.

Even the strongest AI businesses remain exposed to market-wide risks: excessive valuations, rising interest rates, liquidity shocks and a sudden reversal in investor sentiment.

The real winners may not be those making the loudest AI promises, but those quietly using AI to cut costs, expand margins and generate cash flows.

Markets chase stories. Wealth is built on earnings, cash flows and the price you pay.

The biggest danger? Confusing a low-risk business theme with a low-risk investment at any price.

items.title: 🔋 CHINA'S BATTERY CHAIN IS PRINTING RECORD PROFITS. INDIA IS SPENDING BILLIONS TRYING TO COMPETE! 🇨🇳🇮🇳 Look at these two Citi charts. ...
items.description_html:
🔋 CHINA'S BATTERY CHAIN IS PRINTING RECORD PROFITS. INDIA IS SPENDING BILLIONS TRYING TO COMPETE! 🇨🇳🇮🇳

Look at these two Citi charts. 👇

📈 China's battery value-chain EBIT hit a record RMB 64bn in 2Q26, up 6% QoQ.

🔋 Battery makers (ex-BYD) now capture nearly 45% of industry profits, versus lithium miners dominating in 2022.

🏭 And capex is accelerating again!

This isn't just a profit recovery. It's a shift in economic power from MINES to FACTORIES.

Meanwhile, India is committing ₹18,100 crore in PLI incentives to build its battery ecosystem.

THE IRONY?

Cheap Chinese batteries accelerate India's EV revolution but threaten the economics of India's own gigafactories.

🇨🇳 China has SCALE, TECHNOLOGY & INTEGRATION.

🇮🇳 India has AMBITION, INCENTIVES & CATCHING UP TO DO.

China is fighting for market share and margins. India is still fighting to establish manufacturing scale.

The question isn't whether India can manufacture batteries.

It's whether India can manufacture them PROFITABLY against China.

Gigawatts don't create wealth. ROIC does.

items.description_html:
🇮🇳 India's Next Banking Risk May Not Be Bad Loans. It Could Be Good Borrowers Taking on Too Much Debt.

For years, India's consumer credit story was about bringing more people into the formal banking system.

Now the story is changing. Existing borrowers are taking on more debt, often faster than their incomes are growing.

📈 Household debt: 46% of GDP.

💳 Non-mortgage borrowings: 27% of GDP, up from around 16% in 2019.

⚠️ Leveraged borrowers' share of new loan originations: 5% in FY17 → 18% in FY24 → 15% in FY26.

But there's an interesting contradiction.

✅ One-year personal loan default rates improved from 0.51% to 0.35%.

RBI's tighter lending norms appear to be helping contain credit risks, even as household leverage remains elevated.

For banks and NBFCs, the next challenge isn't simply growing loan books. It's ensuring borrowers' incomes can support that growth.

The real question: Are Indian banks lending to more creditworthy customers, or lending more to the same customers?

items.title: RT Paul Bonnet: AMD acquires World Labs for ~$8.2b. But who gets the 💰? My usual breakdown below 👇 From founding to an $8.2b exit in ~2.5 years....
items.description_html:
RT Paul Bonnet
AMD acquires World Labs for ~$8.2b. But who gets the 💰? My usual breakdown below 👇

From founding to an $8.2b exit in ~2.5 years. A huge value creation event. This is a fantastic exit, especially for the co-founders and the team.

Investors will still share ~$2.3b of profits on $1.2b invested, a ~2.9x blended. Low-ish because most of the capital came in last. But it hides a lot of disparity between the various rounds!

So let's dive in:

1) The real home run: founders and team 🏆🥳

This is one of the best founder outcomes I've modelled.

@drfeifei, Justin Johnson, Christoph Lassner and Ben Mildenhall started World Labs in Apr-24. Less than 2.5 years later, they and the team still own ~56% according to my estimates. At an $8.2b valuation, that's a total prize of ~$4.6b to share between them.

Taking a 15% attributed option pool, that's ~$1.2b for the team and ~$3.4b for the four co-founders. If split equally, that's ~$850m each, in just two and a half years. 💸

And, at close, Fei-Fei Li joins AMD as EVP and Chief Scientist, reporting to Lisa Su! Legendary.

2) The buyer was already on the cap table (again) 🔁

AMD Ventures invested in the Series B and the Series C here. Now they are buying the whole company. It's the same playbook as Nvidia with Hugging Face: strategic corporates are using their venture arms as a free option on future acquisitions.

3) The standout VC winners: a16z and Radical Ventures 👑

Both backed Fei-Fei at inception, in Apr-24 at a ~$300m valuation. That Series A will return ~19x the money, or ~$1.2b of proceeds, in under 2.5 years.

Congrats to @martin_casado and team. Another mega win after Cursor and OpenRouter. The team at @a16z truly is on a generational run.

4) The star angels did well 🌟

The Sep-24 Series B had arguably the strongest AI angel list ever assembled: Geoffrey Hinton, Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, Eric Schmidt, Reid Hoffman, Marc Benioff, Ram Shriram and more.

Priced at $1.3b, it was never going to be a 1,000x. But ~5x in two years is a ~125% IRR 📈

And the best part is: Hinton's AlexNet won the 2012 ImageNet competition, and ImageNet was the dataset Fei-Fei built. Twelve years later, he backed her company. Full circle. 🔄

5) The late money: a great IRR, but a poor multiple of money 🤏

The $1b Series C in Feb-26 at $5.4b returns ~1.5x in 7 months. That's a great IRR, but in terms of venture returns, this is a poor multiple of money. Although I am sure no one will complain about seeing DPI this quickly!

Congrats to all involved!
